title: Energy Expenditure Measurements Using Oxymax Protocol
author: Patrick Tso
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xi9fkh6
materials: On the “Manage Databench” screen, select Add Experiment

steps.title: Pre-Experimental Preparation
steps.instruction: Perform initial animal assessments and prepare the Oxymax chambers.

substeps.instruction: Take body composition via NMR before starting the experiment.
Weigh animals and place them into Oxymax chambers.
Supply food and water.
Ensure chamber lids are clasped firmly and evenly.

steps.title: Maintain Drierite and Soda Lime
steps.instruction: Inspect and replace desiccants if necessary: replace Drierite if pink and Soda Lime if not white.

substeps.instruction: Remove canister from holder and unscrew the lid.
Remove spring, metal lid, and cotton filter.
Empty old material and replace with new, ensuring not to fill past the top hole in the canister.
Tap the bottom of the canister to tamp down the material.
Reassemble in order: cotton filter, metal disc, spring, then screw on the top.
Push the canister back onto the holder.

steps.title: System Power-Up and Initialization
steps.instruction: Power on the hardware and initialize the Oxymax software.

substeps.instruction: Turn on all surge protectors and verify power lights are on; ensure PC is powered on and logged in.
Run Oxymax for Windows and select the appropriate hardware configuration.
Allow the system to perform a system scan; if errors occur, check hardware and select 'Refresh'.
Allow approximately 2 hours of warm-up time before calibration or starting an experiment.

steps.title: Prepare for Gas Sensor Calibration
steps.instruction: Configure calibration gas settings and hardware flow.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to 'Tools >> Calibration' (before experiment) or 'Experiment >> Calibration' (after experiment).
Verify calibration gas concentrations: 20.50% Oxygen, 0.50% Carbon Dioxide, balanced with Nitrogen (Primary Standard Grade or better).
Click 'Cal Gas', update concentrations for 'Span' gases (leave 'Zero' gases at 0), select 'Apply', then 'Close'.
Set the sample flow meter on the System Sample Pump to approximately 400 mL/min (indicator ball on top of the .4 L/min line).
Set the outlet pressure on the calibration gas tank regulator between 5-10 PSI.
Insert the calibration gas tank tube into the open T-fitting end of the calibration sample tube on the back of the sample pump; verify noticeable gas flow from the exhaust tube.

steps.title: Calibrate Oxygen Sensor
steps.instruction: Perform the O2 sensor calibration procedure.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Calibrate' button under the 'O2' header.
Confirm sample flow is ~400 mL/min and cal gas pressure is 5-10 PSI with exhaust flow.
Click 'NEXT' to purge the sensor with cal gas.
When the target O2 concentration is displayed, use 'Course Gain' and 'Fine Gain' knobs to match the displayed value to the target (wait a few minutes for lag time until values turn green).
Click 'Next' and then 'Finish'.

steps.title: Calibrate Carbon Dioxide Sensor
steps.instruction: Perform the CO2 sensor calibration procedure.

substeps.instruction: Click the 'Calibrate' button under the 'CO2' header.
Ensure cal gas is on and the Soda Lime column is WHITE (replace if not white).
Click 'NEXT' to purge the sensor; the system will measure the 'Zero' point.
Allow the system to purge the 'Span' gas and measure the necessary gain.
Review the calculated offset and gain, turn off the cal gas flow, and click 'Finish'.
Note: Do not recalibrate between fed and fasting cycles.

steps.title: Configure Experiment Settings
steps.instruction: Set up the experiment parameters and subject roster in the software.

substeps.instruction: Select a configuration template via 'File >> Open Experiment Configuration' (choose mouse or rat configuration).
Fill out the subject roster via 'Experiment >> Setup': enable/disable chambers, enter body weights, and enter info (gender, color, genotype, age, treatment) in the 'Label=Information' field.
Set fresh air flow: Mice (~20g: 0.50 LPM; ~30g: 0.60 LPM); Rats (~200g: 2.0 LPM; ~600g: 3.5 LPM).
Specify a 'Data Filename' location on the hard disk.
Verify settings in 'Experiment >> Properties': set Intervals (0 for indefinite), Cage/Reference Settle (90), and Cage/Reference Measure (30).
Choose the reference method and set Volume Rate Units to mL/kg/min.

steps.title: Run and Monitor Experiment
steps.instruction: Execute the experiment and verify real-time data accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Experiment >> Run'.
Verify initial readings: O2in ~20.94%, CO2in ~0.04%, and RER between 0.7 and 1.0.
Right-click tabs (VO2, VCO2, RER, Heat, etc.) to set the furthest decimal place to 0.00000.

steps.title: Stop Experiment and Export Data
steps.instruction: Safely terminate the run and generate data files.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Experiment >> Stop'.
When exiting the program, select 'Yes' to turn off fresh air only if all animals have been removed from chambers.
Open the desired .CDTA file via 'File >> Open Experiment Data'.
Click 'File >> Generate Subject CSVs' to create CSV files for all subjects.

steps.title: Clean Chambers
steps.instruction: Sanitize equipment using approved cleaners to avoid damaging acrylic.

substeps.instruction: Wipe/rinse chambers and plastic mesh grates using only a mild bleach solution or Clorox Wipes (DO NOT use Sani-Cloth Plus wipes on acrylic).
Remove water bottles by loosening the nut; empty and wash bottles (do not use Sani-Cloths on plastic bottles).
Wipe metal spigots with bleach or Sani-Cloths and rinse with H2O.
Wipe lids thoroughly, ensuring Sani-Cloths do not touch acrylic/plastic parts.
Allow chambers to dry completely before replacing lids.

steps.title: Analyze Data using CLAX
steps.instruction: Use the CLAX program for advanced data visualization and export.

substeps.instruction: Launch CLAX and select 'Add Experiment' on the 'Manage Databench' screen to open files.
Use the 'Experiments' tab to view hardware/experiment configurations and set light/dark cycle times.
Use the 'Subjects' tab to view weights and add grouping 'Tags' (genotype, color, etc.) via 'Create Tag'.
Use the 'Measurements' tab to create new equations.
Access raw data via the 'Data' icon to view specific parameters, individual animals, or all animals.
Export data to Excel or Prism using 'Export and Copy to Clipboard'.
Utilize Statistics, Time Graphs, Box Plot, Histogram, and Correlation tools for visualization.
